title: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

sense.text:
“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail.” That is speaking of the prophecies. The prophecies that are written, none of them shall fail: whatever the Lord spake shall come to pass. Many of them have already come to pass, and many more are yet to come.

We are less than two months from blitzing the earth for Passover. Wherever our people are, the curses of Deuteronomy 28 are on them, and whoever can read with spiritual eyes cannot help but know who the biblical Jews, the real Israelites, are. Babylon’s religion is spread throughout the whole earth, so the same lies told to us here are told to our brothers and sisters wherever they are scattered. The difference is the spirit the Lord put on the men here in America to go to the four corners of the earth and teach, and recover the lost sheep.

“Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God”: in the feast of unleavened bread, the feast of weeks and the feast of tabernacles, “and they shall not appear before the Lord empty.” The feast of weeks is the feast we are going into now, Pentecost. These scriptures are for those who are new and are just finding out who they are, and it is always good to go over these things again, because repetition is the father of mastery.

precepts.why:
“Even after a certain rate every day, offering according to the commandment of Moses, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts, three times in the year, even in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles.”

Again the same three feasts. We are supposed to gather and give an offering three times a year. We come together.

We do not give a physical offering today. So what do we offer? We offer ourselves, we offer obedience: “He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.” Keeping the law is the offering we bring before the Lord at the feasts.

“Now when I was come home again, and my wife Anna was restored unto me, with my son Tobias, in the feast of Pentecost, which is the holy feast of the seven weeks.”

This scripture explains what Pentecost is: “the holy feast of the seven weeks.” Pentecost is the feast of weeks of Deuteronomy 16.

“And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.” That feast of Pentecost in the New Testament was the feast of weeks. We are going into that same feast now, on a double Sabbath.

sense.text:
Anthropology is the study of humanity, of societies and people, and cultural anthropology studies a people’s meaning, their norms and values. Our people are hardly ever out there; it is the other nations, especially Esau, who get to go out and dig up the historical artifacts.

“That they may shoot in secret at the perfect.” We are the perfect. “Suddenly do they shoot at him, and fear not.”

“They encourage themselves in an evil matter.” “They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search: both the inward thought of every one of them, and the heart, is deep.”

This is when they go and do their studies and their research. They find out our history and they know. They study us so they can figure out what drives us and what motivates us: basically how to make us sin. That is what they are ultimately trying to do, to keep us in the midst of sin.

Inclusivism says there is beauty in the variety of different schools of thought and that they can coexist. It stands in contrast to exclusivism, which says only one way is true and all others are erroneous. This is what exclusivism is.

“When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel.” The Lord separated the sons of Adam.

“For the Lord’s portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.” And no one else. Everyone else is excluded. They don’t like to hear that; they say it’s neither Jew nor Greek. But it is what it is.

precepts.why: It is the same in the New Testament: “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” That is exclusive. No one else is included in that. Christ came for Jacob, the Lord’s portion, and for no one else.

sense.text:
The coexist image was made by a Polish graphic designer in 2000 for an art competition about dialogue, understanding and coexistence. It puts the symbols together: the crescent and star of Islam, the peace sign, the male and female sign, the star they call Judaism, Wicca, Taoism, Confucianism (confusion) and Christianity, and says all of these are supposed to coexist.

That star is not Judaism; it is the star of Molech. They try to call it the star of David. “Yea, ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them: and I will carry you away beyond Babylon.” Those figures were made to be worshipped, and for it Israel was carried away.

This is where the title comes from. The scribes and Pharisees ask, “Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.” Christ answers, “Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition?”

That is what we ask Christians all the time. Why are you not keeping a Sabbath day? Why aren’t the women dressing modestly? Why do you eat unclean foods? And these are just some of the basic laws.

“Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.” So you children at home putting your hands on your mama or your daddy: Christ said, let him die the death.

“Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition.” They made the commandments of God null and void by keeping their traditions. That is modern day Christianity: by their traditions they make the commandments of God of none effect. Like the Sabbath day: by their traditions they do not honour the Sabbath day.

“Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying, This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.” They are very good at quoting scriptures and very good at talking about the love of Jesus, but their heart is far from the Lord.

“But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.” The doctrines they teach are the commandments of men.

The man-made religions show it: John Smyth and the Baptist religion, Joseph Smith and the Mormon religion, William Miller and the Seventh Day Adventists, Charles Taze Russell and the Jehovah’s Witnesses, Charles Parham and the Pentecostal religion. These are the doctrines of men our Christian brothers and sisters are following.

Then there is what they call contextualization: making Christianity relevant to a culture without addressing the doctrine, changing only the style of worship. But the doctrine is right where our people are falling off the horse, and Christianity is all about the praise and worship team. They took their European music and building styles into other parts of the world, and built churches, sang songs and prayed in a local ethnic style to appeal to the ones they were trying to win over. That is why they are always in our neighborhoods.

precepts.why: What are they supposed to be teaching? “For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.” The doctrine is keeping the laws of God. That is the good doctrine; the commandments of men are not.

sense.text: Those who hold an exclusivist religion see syncretism as corrupting the original religion, and that is our religion: our forefathers fought to keep it separate. Mattathias answered with a loud voice: “Though all the nations that are under the king’s dominion obey him, and fall away every one from the religion of their fathers, and give consent to his commandments.”

“Yet will I and my sons and my brethren walk in the covenant of our fathers. God forbid that we should forsake the law and the ordinances. We will not hearken to the king’s words, to go from our religion, either on the right hand, or the left.”

Our religion is keeping the commandments.

Eleazar considered “the excellency of his ancient years, and the honour of his gray head”, “or rather the holy law made and given by God: therefore he answered accordingly, and willed them straightways to send him to the grave.”

“For it becometh not our age, said he, in any wise to dissemble, whereby many young persons might think that Eleazar, being fourscore years old and ten, were now gone to a strange religion.” Ninety years old, and he would not be seen going to a strange religion, because we have to be examples to the younger generation.

precepts.why:
This is what Eleazar was doing. “I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised the Lord with songs. And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crowns.” That young man is Christ.

“These be they that have put off the mortal clothing, and put on the immortal, and have confessed the name of God: now are they crowned, and receive palms.” “It is the Son of God, whom they have confessed in the world. Then began I greatly to commend them that stood so stiffly for the name of the Lord.”

Eleazar was not going to go against the commandments of God, which is our religion. He stood stiffly, and that is how the crown is received.

sense.text: Judas Maccabeus went privily into the towns, called his kinsfolks together, “and took unto them all such as continued in the Jews’ religion.” The Jews’ religion: keeping the commandments of God.
“And also pity the temple profaned of ungodly men.” Those other nations are ungodly men.

These are those that stand stiffly. Seven brethren and their mother were “compelled by the king against the law to taste swine’s flesh.” Now why is it that swine’s flesh is all throughout the black church? And they run to Colossians for it, but that is not what Colossians is talking about.

“We are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of our fathers.” That is standing stiffly, that is getting your crown. Do you know what level of faith that is? You truly cannot desire anything left in this world. We are already captives: bills, working fourteen hours a day. What are you leaving? There has got to be something better.

The king in a rage cut out the tongue of the first, cut off the utmost parts of his body, and had him “fried in the pan”, his brethren and mother looking on. They exhorted one another “to die manfully”, saying, “The Lord God looketh upon us, and in truth hath comfort in us.” Then they asked the second, “Wilt thou eat, before thou be punished throughout every member of thy body?” That is the arrogance of the wicked when the earth is given into their hand and they have the power to speak proudly.
“But he answered in his own language, and said, No.” At the last gasp he said, “the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, unto everlasting life.”

The third “put out his tongue, and that right soon, holding forth his hands manfully.” He just put his hands out: let’s get this over with. “These I had from heaven; and for his laws I despise them; and from him I hope to receive them again.”

“Insomuch that the king, and they that were with him, marvelled at the young man’s courage, for that he nothing regarded the pains.” They marvelled because there was a certain spirit in them. There was something they knew that the heathen did not: that there is only one living God.

The fourth said, “It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him: as for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life.” Imagine the look on his face. Before they tortured him he had a message: there is no resurrection for you, no hope for you.

The fifth said, “Thou hast power over men, thou art corruptible, thou doest what thou wilt; yet think not that our nation is forsaken of God.” Because he said, I will never leave thee nor forsake thee. “But abide a while, and behold his great power, how he will torment thee and thy seed.”

The sixth said, “we suffer these things for ourselves, having sinned against our God.” So we understand why we are going through this. “But think not thou, that takest in hand to strive against God, that thou shalt escape unpunished.” They will not escape unpunished.

The mother saw her seven sons slain in one day and “bare it with a good courage, because of the hope that she had in the Lord.” She said, “I cannot tell how ye came into my womb”, but “the Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, and found out the beginning of all things, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again, as ye now regard not your own selves for his laws’ sake.”

What kind of mercy would it be for the same people who torment us like this to get an equal reward in the kingdom? That is not a merciful God, to allow them to do that to us and then give them the same portion. Somebody needed to hear this, to build up their spirit and their strength.

precepts.why: Why did they marvel? “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.” All the gods of the nations are idols, so the nations have no living God. That is why the young man’s courage was a marvel to them.

“For though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, (as there be gods many, and lords many,) But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.”

We understand that there is only one living God. That is why they marvelled: the brethren were looking to the one God who would raise them up, and the king had none.

sense.text: Razis, one of the elders of Jerusalem, was “a lover of his countrymen.” That is nationalism. That is loving your race. He was “a man of very good report, who for his kindness was called a father of the Jews.”

“For in the former times, when they mingled not themselves with the Gentiles”: that is religious exclusivism. “He had been accused of Judaism, and did boldly jeopard his body and life with all vehemency for the religion of the Jews.”

precepts.why:
You might think that changed in the New Testament with Jesus. They love Galatians: “For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews’ religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it.” So we read about the Jews’ religion in the New Testament. Nothing changed. That persecuting is read in Acts the ninth chapter.

“And profited in the Jews’ religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers.” The same religion Razis jeoparded his body for.

Paul says, “after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee. And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers.” Who are our fathers? “Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come.”

The Christians come up to us on the street talking about Jews and Gentiles. But where do you read about the other tribes in the New Testament? You read of Anna of Asher in Luke, and of Naphtali and Zebulun, but all the tribes are not named. Here Paul says, our twelve tribes. The religion of the Jews belonged to all twelve tribes, and Paul was still in it.

sense.text: “James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad.” Paul said our twelve tribes, and James writes to the twelve tribes: Paul and James are on one accord. So how is it that they say Paul is teaching don’t keep the commandments, but they don’t accuse James of that?

“Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.” And “If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.”

“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” That man with the wavering spirit, who asks not in faith: “let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.” Don’t let him think he is going to receive anything from the Lord. “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.”

The Catholic Church in Central and South America has taken in elements of the indigenous peoples of the Americas, the ones we read about in 2 Esdras, and of the enslaved Africans, so long as they are remade to conform to a Christian worldview. The image of Our Lady of Guadalupe is one of them. Their prayer to her is said in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit (the Trinity) and asks her to make intercession for the church. That would make her the mediator.

But Christ is the one: “But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood. Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.” Christ makes intercession for us, not a woman. That is woman worship, the same thing Paul had to address in the church of Corinth, the same spirit of Diana coming back up.

The prayer calls her the ever virgin Mary, and they teach she never had sex. This is what has happened to our brothers in the northern kingdom: they got conquered, and this is the modern form of Christianity they are under.

“Is not this the carpenter’s son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas? And his sisters, are they not all with us?” Mary did not just have Jesus. She had other children. Joseph was getting it in.

So the Roman Catholic doctrines about Mary, the immaculate conception and the assumption of Mary, are a lie by the scriptures. She had a lot of kids. Esau is crafty: he makes you comfortable in his bastard religion, mixed with the local customs, so you feel like you are serving God, and it looks nothing like the original Christian church we read about in Acts.

The Latter-day Saints say truth in other sources can be identified by personal revelation. That is: this is my truth; I’m not religious, I’m spiritual; the Bible says this to me, it might say that to you. Here is the truth: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” The law is the truth.

precepts.why: In the New Testament: “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.” Thy word is truth, the same as the law is the truth. There is no personal truth apart from it.

And what is the word? “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.” The law and the testimony is what the word of God is. That crosses the t’s and dots the i’s: the law is the truth, the word is truth, and the word is the law and the testimony.

sense.text: They talk about personal revelation: the Lord told me, he came to me, only me. That is what you get in a Christian church, the pastor saying twenty people are going to give two thousand in the next twenty minutes. What the hell is this? Lock the doors. “Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation.”
“For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.” Holy men of God spake, as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.

precepts.why:
Moved by the Holy Ghost: “Of which salvation the prophets have enquired and searched diligently.” “Searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify, when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow.”

What was in the prophets? The Spirit of Christ which was in them. The Spirit of Christ was in the prophets.

“These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.”

All the things written in the law, the prophets and the psalms were written by men who had the Spirit of Christ on them. So why do they ask us why we are reading out of the Old Testament? That is the effect of Christianity and the blending of religions. And practicing that modern form of Christianity is going to lead you straight to damnation.

sense.text: All we have been dealing with goes into serving other gods: idolatry. “I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt have no other gods before me.” But what we have been reading is a mix, a blending of religions and other gods, from the beginning.

“Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me.”
“And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.” That means there are going to be those, like us, who are going to repent in these last days.
“Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.”

“Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.” These are the first four commandments, and they go into: love the Lord thy God. All of this blending of religions is meant to take you away from serving the Lord thy God. How many of these religions know how to honour the Sabbath day? How many of these Christians are going to keep the feast of tabernacles, the feast of weeks, Passover? It is meant to keep you in sin.

precepts.why:
What it is to take the Lord’s name in vain: “Remove far from me vanity and lies.” “Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.”

We are a holy people; he put his spirit in us, and we carry his name. So when they say you can’t keep the commandments, why can’t we? That does not mean we have never sinned; St. John says all men have sinned, and whoever says he has not is a liar. But when they say you can’t keep the commandments, it is because they want to remain in their sins.

“Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.”

The first four commandments are how to love the Lord thy God; all the others are how to love thy neighbour as thyself. The focus here is the first: no other gods before him.

“Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God is one Lord: And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart.”

One Lord, loved with all the heart. Blending in other gods is breaking the first and great commandment.

sense.text: Syncretism is the blending of diverse religious beliefs, traditions or practices into a combined system, and it comes by assimilation, migration or conquest. Here are biblical examples of that blending. “And the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods. And Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor.” Baal-peor is another god. That was willingly: the blending can be willing or it can be forced. “And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.”
“And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and served Baalim.”

“And they forsook the Lord God of their fathers, which brought them out of the land of Egypt, and followed other gods.” You see the theme. When you do not love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, you are going to break the other commandments too; you are not going to love your neighbour as yourself either. This is the first step, breaking away from the commandments and purposely aligning yourself against the Lord.

“Of the gods of the people that were round about them, and bowed themselves unto them, and provoked the Lord to anger.” That is the proximity: being close to those nations, we started to follow their gods.

Still the proximity, dwelling close to those nations. “Take heed to thyself that thou be not snared by following them, after that they be destroyed from before thee; and that thou enquire not after their gods, saying, How did these nations serve their gods? even so will I do likewise.” Is that not what our people do here in America, and wherever we are scattered?

“For every abomination to the Lord, which he hateth, have they done unto their gods.” Everything he hates, they have done to their gods, and if you go after them you are going to be just like them. “For even their sons and their daughters they have burnt in the fire to their gods.” Abortions. You are going to do the same thing.

“But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh.” When you turn against the Lord, you turn against your neighbour, because he is taking foreign women. It turns your heart from following the Lord, and you hate your brother.

“Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods.” He had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, “and his wives turned away his heart.” “For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father.”

“For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.” Now he is going after the other gods. He built a high place for Chemosh and for Molech, “And likewise did he for all his strange wives, which burnt incense and sacrificed unto their gods.”

precepts.why:
“Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe.” He calls interracial marriage whoredom.

“For we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children.”

“Now therefore, my son, love thy brethren, and despise not in thy heart thy brethren, the sons and daughters of thy people, in not taking a wife of them.” Taking a strange woman is despising your brethren. That is how Solomon’s strange wives were a turning against his neighbour as well as against the Lord.

sense.text:
Jeroboam feared that if the people went up to sacrifice in Jerusalem their heart would turn again to Rehoboam, so he “made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” He set one in Beth-el and the other in Dan, “And this thing became a sin.”

This became sin unto the northern kingdom. Every king after him who did the same thing was compared back to Jeroboam.

precepts.why:
“They have set up kings, but not by me: they have made princes, and I knew it not: of their silver and their gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off. Thy calf, O Samaria, hath cast thee off; mine anger is kindled against them.” Jeroboam’s calves are the calf of Samaria.

But remember, it was all twelve tribes that made the calf when Moses went up into the mount. All twelve tribes were there, so we all have that in common.

sense.text: Manasseh did “after the abominations of the heathen”. “For he built up again the high places which Hezekiah his father had destroyed.” He went back and served the same gods at the same altars his father destroyed.
He built altars in the house of the Lord, “and dealt with familiar spirits and wizards: he wrought much wickedness in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.”

He set a graven image of the grove in the house where the Lord put his name, though the Lord had promised Israel the land “only if they will observe to do according to all that I have commanded them”. “But they hearkened not: and Manasseh seduced them to do more evil than did the nations whom the Lord destroyed before the children of Israel.” We went crazier than the heathen.

Ezekiel is brought to Jerusalem, “where was the seat of the image of jealousy, which provoketh to jealousy.” “Seest thou what they do? even the great abominations that the house of Israel committeth here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary?” The Lord is saying, I’m out, I can’t be around y’all.

“And behold every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall round about.” That is like putting the images of Cesare Borgia on the walls, Guadalupe on the walls.

“Hast thou seen what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.” What do you do in the dark? Your secrets, your secret sins.

precepts.why:
What were they putting on the walls? Images of the gods of their enemies. “For when she saw men pourtrayed upon the wall, the images of the Chaldeans pourtrayed with vermilion.” “And as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea.”

That is why the Lord said that with your eyes you will go a whoring, when he gave us the fringes.

“And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” The ancients did it in the dark because their deeds were evil.

sense.text:
The Assyrian and Babylonian kings took conquered peoples out of their lands and scattered them, for control, assimilation, labour, demographic engineering and punishment. They did the same to us here in slavery, splitting the families up and sending them to different plantations, and now you have ICE. Then came Hellenization, the spread of Greek culture after Alexander, a forced assimilation that blended Greek traditions with local customs into a syncretic culture. In Alexandria citizenship depended on your religion; Jews could not lead in festivals or hold public office unless they converted to paganism. So when you see our people running for political office, they do the same thing, and many marry Esau.

Alexander “reigned in his stead, the first over Greece” and “took spoils of many nations”, then “parted his kingdom among them”: his generals Ptolemy, Cassander, Seleucus and Lysimachus. The Seleucid portion was the largest. When Paul was going to these places, he was going to see us: Israelites had been conquered and were there from the time of the Greeks.

King Antiochus wrote “that all should be one people, And every one should leave his laws”. “Yea, many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.”
They were to “profane the sabbaths and festival days”, the same thing that is going on today, and “sacrifice swine’s flesh, and unclean beasts”.

“To the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances.” And the law is our religion; that is why verse 43 says many of the Israelites “consented to his religion.” “And whosoever would not do according to the commandment of the king, he said, he should die.”

precepts.why:
“Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.” If you could not profess yourself to be a Jew, then you would be a Gentile.

“The Jews were compelled to go in procession to Bacchus, carrying ivy.” Compelled means forced. Now we do it willingly. A decree went out that they “should observe the same fashions, and be partakers of their sacrifices.”

sense.text:
Christianity and Islam are bullies of the African culture: you must become European before you can be a Christian. And the Christian who says Mormonism teaches Jesus and Lucifer are brothers says Father, Son and Holy Spirit fast, like the fine print, the side effects read fast. Esau is a born liar. So who is Lucifer?

“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” Lucifer weakened the nations. “I will be like the most High.” “They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms.”

Lucifer is a man. He is not an angel that fell down and got kicked out of heaven, and all that crazy stuff.

This is the scripture for the preacher who says Israel was chosen not because they are favored, and calls the people in the land over there Israel. “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth? Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.”

“Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” When the young girl asked about Israel, he spoke as though the people over there are Israel. That is the slander: then who are we?
“Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” The Lord is setting us in order before their eyes.

The Three Kings Day is rooted in syncretism: Spain brought it to Puerto Rico in colonization and they made it their own. They take ownership of it as if they are serving God. Our enemies give us something and we put a little salt on it to make it better than what they have, the way Manasseh did more evil than the heathen. And the preacher who says truth can change: that is what religious syncretism does to us. And the coexist sign: if that were really true, why are the Israelis bombing the Palestinians? They don’t want them to coexist.

“Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.” These traditions are not after Christ.

precepts.why:
This is what Christ quoted in Matthew 15. “For the Lord hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep, and hath closed your eyes”, and the vision is “as the words of a book that is sealed.” “Wherefore the Lord said, Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men.”

All these wicked men with their different religions. Christianity has done a hell of a number on our people; it has destroyed many of our people. That is why we are going to continue to hit these streets, travel, study, bring out these classes, and do the work until Christ returns.

sense.text: “For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.” With all these religions and doctrines of men, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.
“And to this agree the words of the prophets.” What spirit was in the prophets? Christ. So the words of the prophets agree, because the Spirit of Christ spoke in them.

“After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up.” “Known unto God are all his works from the beginning of the world.”

precepts.why: “Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” The prophets had the Spirit of Christ in them, and the Lord revealed his secret to them, so the words of the prophets agree with what he does.
